findings.evidence: Verbatim: 'the QA gate also gains new preconditions this release -- an epic cannot proceed to implementation without `design-satisfied` plus a bound `design_artifact`, and cannot approve without a coherent rollup'. Present at HEAD:62 and UNCHANGED by this diff (git diff -U0 -- CHANGELOG.md shows one hunk, @@ -19 +19,36 @@). DP1 at docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:807, edited in this same change set, withdraws exactly this claim: 'An earlier version of this row claimed implementation orchestration "cannot begin" without `design-satisfied` and a bound `design_artifact` reference'. The code: design-gate-precheck's own help (qa-gate.sh:4215-4229) says it is 'a PRE-DELEGATION convenience the orchestrator MAY run ... never enforced from here (nothing can force a prompt to run a script before deciding to delegate)'; DP1's own Verification-method column says 'enforced at `approve`, not `enter`'; and approve's design-satisfied refusal is waivable with --no-design.
findings.description: The corrected-table-versus-uncorrected-prose contradiction, on the primary release surface. Wrong three ways: (a) under opt-in an epic CAN proceed to implementation with no design at all; (b) the approve-time refusal is waivable; (c) it asserts a PRE-implementation enforcement point that does not exist in any form. It is not covered by the opt-in preface at :21-22, which disclaims 'the feature description below' (the paragraph at :56-81) -- this sits in 'Why this is a major' (:83-103), a normative argument whose premise it is.

findings.evidence: The narrowed claim reads 'a design that was STARTED must be SATISFIED before `approve` will pass'. --no-design is a GENERAL bypass of the whole design-satisfied refusal, not one scoped to no_design_attempted. Proof, all re-run at 897b7fe: `grep -n 'bypass_design=' .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh` -> exactly two sites, 5269 (local bypass_design=0) and 5423 (inside the `--no-design)` arm), so nothing else can set it; cmd_approve's DESIGN-SATISFIED-REFUSAL block (:7068-7079) is `if [ "$bypass_design" = "1" ]; then <obs only>; else compute_design_satisfied; ... fi`, and compute_design_satisfied is the sole producer of DESIGN_SATISFIED_KEY, so design_not_satisfied / design_verdict_missing / design_verdict_stale cannot fire under the flag; the arm's own recorded text says it 'bypasses ONLY the satisfied-verdict requirement'. The only refusal --no-design cannot waive is design_conflict_open (:7083+, unconditional), which is a filed DESIGN-CONFLICT record, not a design-review verdict. No test asserts the started-design case refuses under --no-design; design-artifact.test.sh:1042 and :1131 drive approve --no-design on tasks that DO carry DESIGN-ARTIFACT records and expect success.
findings.description: DP1 is rated PROVEN and its whole purpose this cycle was to state the mandatory-versus-audited-exit boundary precisely. As written it asserts an asymmetry the code does not implement (design-less -> audited exit; design-started -> mandatory), overclaiming enforcement -- the same family the ledger corrects elsewhere. Fix: 'must be SATISFIED before approve will pass, OR waived by an audited --no-design <reason> recorded in the approval comment; the flag is not scoped to the design-less case', or move the row to PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT.

findings.evidence: 'Two of the checks the design phase adds are not yet trustworthy in a target project.' The other figures DO verify exactly: `wc -c .../flagship/docs/specs/target-23z.md` -> 49512, and `shasum -a 256` on it -> 8446ae41...f4f3b, byte-identical to the design_hash on the satisfied DESIGN-REVIEW v1 verdict, so it is the reviewed artifact and not a later revision; three DESIGN-REVIEW v1 records (16:33:45Z needs_revision, 17:46:02Z needs_revision, 18:12:11Z satisfied); target-23z created 2026-09-28T16:03:55Z -> last same-day COMPLETION v1 on target-23z.1 at 19:27:38Z = 3h23m43s, which rounds to the claimed 3h24m; and the flagship approval at 2026-09-29T15:53:25Z binds change_set_hash=e3b0c442...855, the empty-set sentinel, confirming 'did not reach a meaningful approval'.
